claims.text: The funding opportunity supports projects in archaeology, art history, and related fields.
The funding opportunity has specific focus areas determined by benefactors.
The Beatrice di Cardi, Janet Arnold, Tessa and Mortimer Wheeler, and William Lambarde awards have a deadline of April 7th each year.
References for the Beatrice di Cardi, Janet Arnold, Tessa and Mortimer Wheeler, and William Lambarde awards are due by April 14th each year.
The William and Jane Morris Church Conservation grants have two application rounds: March 31st and August 31st annually.
The Hugh Phillips, Margaret and Tom Jones, Wainwright Research Archaeology in Wales, and Open Research awards have a deadline of January 15th each year.
References for the Hugh Phillips, Margaret and Tom Jones, Wainwright Research Archaeology in Wales, and Open Research awards are due by January 21st each year.
The funding opportunity supports research into the material past.
The Society will be the main or a significant financial contributor to funded projects.
Funding is available for projects with definable objectives and specific, measurable outcomes within larger projects.
Applications for projects of archaeological synthesis will be considered.
Early career researchers are welcomed to apply.
Projects that are innovative, entail new initiatives, and/or create interdisciplinary interest are welcomed.
Applications must be from the project director or principal investigator.
Work contributing to an undergraduate or postgraduate degree is not funded.
Retrospective applications are not funded.
Travel to, or attendance at, conferences is not funded.
Eligible project costs include travel and subsistence for the project team.
Eligible project costs include costs of specialist or scientific investigation, and technical services like imaging and illustration.
Eligible project costs include hire of plant and site accommodation.
Eligible project costs include materials and consumables.
Eligible project costs include hire of specialist equipment that the applicant cannot reasonably access.
Ineligible project costs include personal remuneration.
Ineligible project costs include salaries of staff holding current appointments.
Ineligible project costs include institutional overheads.
Ineligible project costs include internal hire charges within the applicant’s institution or between project partners.
Ineligible project costs include publication subventions and publication grants.
Ineligible project costs include contingency estimates.
Awards are typically made on an annual basis with possible renewal for up to two further years, for a maximum of three years.
Projects should not start before April 1st in the year of application.
Grants should be taken up by December 31st of the year in which they are awarded.
Awarding decisions are based on the quality and viability of the research proposal.
Awarding decisions consider how the project aligns with the Society’s strategy and values.
Applications are assessed solely on the information provided on the application form.
A clear articulation of research aims, costings, and proposed duration is required.
A clear statement of the contribution of the proposed research to scholarship is required.
A clear plan for timely publication/dissemination of results is required.
A request for a specific sum and declaration of other funding applications is required.
A statement of the minimum sum needed for project viability is required.
For subsequent applications, a summary of results to date and expenditure statement is required.
Most awards require one or two references.
Successful applicants must demonstrate they have received all relevant permissions before funds are released.
Any unspent award remainder must be returned to the Society.
Successful applicants must submit a report of up to 1,000 words, a financial statement, and images by February 28th of the following year.
Acknowledgement of the research grant in any publication or practical use of the research is required.
Research Awards offer grants of £500 to £5,000 for research into the human past through its material culture or material remains.
The Janet Arnold Awards offer grants of £350 to £5,000 for research on the history of dress and its materials.
The Beatrice de Cardi Awards offer grants of £5,000 to £15,000 for archaeological research in specific regions of the Arabian Gulf and Pakistan.
The Margaret and Tom Jones Awards offer grants of £1,000 to £10,500 for the archaeology of extensive sites or landscapes in the UK.
The Tessa and Mortimer Wheeler Travel Awards offer grants of up to £500 for undergraduate and first-year postgraduate students studying archaeology in the UK to gain fieldwork experience abroad.
The William Lambarde Travel Awards offer grants of up to £500 to support antiquarian or archaeological research.
The William and Jane Morris Church Conservation Grants are between £500 and £5,000.
The Linda Parry Textile Research and Conservation Grants are up to £4,000 per project.
The Marion Wilson Awards are for research projects in southern Britain.
The Joan Pye Awards are for early-career researchers in prehistoric and Roman archaeology in the UK.
The Hugh Chapman Memorial Awards are for research projects on the Western Roman Empire or antiquarian matters in London and its environs.
Applications for the William and Jane Morris Church Conservation Grants must be for work on decorative or non-structural features inside a church, chapel, or place of worship in the UK.
Objects funded by the William and Jane Morris Church Conservation Grants must have been made no later than 1896.
Turret clocks and organs are generally not grant-aided by the William and Jane Morris Church Conservation Grants, but their cases may be considered exceptionally.
The William and Jane Morris Church Conservation Grants do not fund projects outside the UK, structural repairs, fabric maintenance, alterations, decoration, or electrical/plumbing/heating systems.
The William and Jane Morris Church Conservation Grants do not fund works already completed or anything created after 1896.
The William and Jane Morris Church Conservation Grants do not fund items on the outside or in the grounds of a building.
The Linda Parry Textile Research and Conservation Grants fund research and conservation of textiles in churches, chapels, and places of worship in the UK and Crown Dependencies.
Priority for Linda Parry grants is given to projects with greater historical significance and conservation need, especially from local churches.
An organization may submit only one application per round for the Linda Parry grants.
The Linda Parry grants do not fund projects outside the UK or Crown Dependencies, structural repairs, fabric maintenance, alterations, decoration, or electrical/plumbing/heating systems.
The Linda Parry grants do not fund clocks, bells, or organs (with exceptions for cases of antiquarian interest).
The Linda Parry grants do not fund works already completed or anything created after 1896.
The Linda Parry grants do not fund items on the outside or in the grounds of a building.
The Beatrice de Cardi awards are for archaeological research on the United Arab Emirates, the Sultanate of Oman, Saudi Arabia, and the Pakistan province of Balochistan.
The Margaret and Tom Jones awards are for archaeological investigation, excavation, or analysis of large sites or landscapes in the UK from the Neolithic to post-Medieval periods.
The Margaret and Tom Jones awards support the development or testing of methodologies for the field investigation, excavation, or analysis of large sites or landscapes.
The Tessa and Mortimer Wheeler Travel Awards are for undergraduate and first-year postgraduate students studying archaeology at a UK university.
The William Lambarde Travel Awards are for travel to support the applicant's individual research.
The William Lambarde Travel Awards do not consider applications for travel to participate in an established project or as one of multiple funding applications for a larger project.
The William Lambarde Travel Awards do not fund travel for conference attendance.
The Beatrice de Cardi awards consider applications for the analysis and publication of post-excavation materials under specific conditions.
The Beatrice de Cardi awards will pay for the analysis of excavated materials, including dating and laboratory-based analysis, for publication.
The Beatrice de Cardi awards require a clear timetable with milestones and a fully costed plan for publication and dissemination.
The Beatrice de Cardi awards will not pay publication subvention costs.
The Janet Arnold Awards encourage applications that explore dress and its components as material culture in the contexts of colonialism and its legacies.
The Janet Arnold Awards encourage applications that redress narratives characterizing costume as craft or vernacular art.
The Janet Arnold Awards encourage applications that liberate previously unheard voices and explore new approaches to costume studies.
The Janet Arnold Awards encourage applications that explore decolonising museums and their collections with a focus on dress.
Preference will be given to applicants who have not previously received a Janet Arnold Award.
Applicants for Janet Arnold Awards must obtain consent from the owner(s)/custodian(s) of any item(s) to be examined.
Applicants for Janet Arnold Awards must demonstrate they have the skills necessary to undertake the proposed work and that it will not damage the item(s) of dress concerned.
Preference will be given to applicants who have not previously received a Wheeler Award.
The referee for a Wheeler Travel Award must be a supervisor of recognised status and position who has agreed to supervise the grant.

The reference for a Wheeler Travel Award must indicate agreement to be responsible for overseeing the work, comment on the quality and viability of the proposal, and demonstrate an assessment of risks.
Preference will be given to applicants who have not previously received a Lambarde Award.
Applicants for William Lambarde Travel Awards must present as detailed an estimate as possible of travel and associated expenses.
The William and Jane Morris Church Conservation Grants require a professional architect or established conservator to direct the work.
Work funded by the William and Jane Morris Church Conservation Grants must be completed within one year of receipt of the grant.
Completion of work for the William and Jane Morris Church Conservation Grants must be certified by an appropriate professional.
The Linda Parry Textile Research and Conservation Grants require an Icon-accredited conservator to direct the work and certify its completion.
Work funded by the Linda Parry Textile Research and Conservation Grants must be completed within one year of receipt of the grant.
Completion of work for the Linda Parry Textile Research and Conservation Grants must be certified by an appropriate professional.
The Margaret and Tom Jones awards are not open to those previously in receipt of funding for Mucking post-excavation.
The Society has two grant award programmes.
The Society promotes and supports its objectives of conservation, research, and dissemination through its grant award programmes.
